prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val2] 政务服务 · 办理时限 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "事项名称" spans 1 col × 2 row; "办理时限（工作日）" spans 2 col × 1 row; "所需材料" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "事项名称" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 92px
  col 2: header "办理时限（工作日） › 法定" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 31px
  col 3: header "办理时限（工作日） › 承诺" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 4: header "所需材料" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 414px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 480px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare the statutory and promised processing times for each government service item, then see the materials required for that item.","reading":"Readers scan row by row: first identify the service item, then compare the two adjacent time figures (法定 vs 承诺), then read the materials list. The two time columns need to read as a pair under their shared header; the materials column is a long reference list and will wrap.","groups":["Columns 2 and 3 belong together: they are the paired 法定/承诺 values under the shared 办理时限（工作日） header and must stay adjacent for comparison.","Column 1 is the row-identification column and should remain visually separate from the time pair.","Column 4 is an independent reference list; it can be wider or narrower but should not disrupt the time comparison."],"keep_intact":["事项名称 values ideally on one line so rows remain easy to scan","法定 and 承诺 leaf headers","numeric time values 15/1, 20/5, 10/3","办理时限（工作日） group header ideally on one line","material names and their 、 separators; break at separators rather than inside terms"],"may_wrap":["所需材料 lists, which are far wider than any feasible column","事项名称 in a materials-first design","办理时限（工作日） group header if the two time columns are compressed"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[113,80,80,206],"idea":"Balanced: give the row-label column exactly its one-line width and the two time columns enough combined width for the group header, leaving the remainder for materials."},{"name":"B","widths":[104,66,66,243],"idea":"Materials-first: accept wrapped row labels and a two-line time-group header so the material lists get the widest column."},{"name":"C","widths":[120,64,64,231],"idea":"Row-label-first with a compressed time pair: keep every item name on one line, let the shared time header wrap, and still give materials more width than the balanced design."}]}
